sections.intro: Rope access is a safe, fast, and cost-effective way to carry out building work at height.

sections.title: Advantages of Rope Access
sections.imageAlt: Rope access technicians on a louvred facade

items.title: Fast and Efficient
items.text: Rope access lets our technicians move freely around the building, saving the time needed to erect and dismantle scaffolding — faster cleaning without compromising quality.

items.title: Proven Safety
items.text: Certified technicians work with standard safety equipment and twin-rope systems.

items.title: Cost Saving
items.text: No scaffolding or extra gondolas means a more efficient budget.

items.title: Suits Any Building
items.text: Offices, apartments, hotels, and facades with complex shapes.

sections.title: Our Rope Access Cleaning Process
sections.imageAlt: Rope access technician working at height

items.title: Site Survey & Consultation
items.text: We survey the building to assess cleaning needs and surfaces and choose the best tools and techniques.

items.title: Planning & Scheduling
items.text: Work is scheduled to avoid disrupting building activity.

items.title: Rope Access Cleaning
items.text: Technicians work systematically from top to bottom with safe equipment and cleaning agents.

items.title: Supervision & Quality Control
items.text: A supervisor checks the result in every area.

items.title: Completion & Report
items.text: A report with documentation is handed to building management.

sections.title: Safety Is Our Priority
sections.text: We understand the importance of safety when working at height. Inland applies the highest safety standards on every building cleaning project. Our technicians are fully equipped with protective gear and follow strict safety procedures to protect themselves and everyone around them.

items.a: Rope access is a method of working at height using twin-rope systems, letting technicians reach building facades without scaffolding or gondolas.

items.q: What work can be done with rope access?
items.a: Glass and facade cleaning, glass sealant installation and repair, painting, and facade inspection and repair.
Usually, yes — there is no scaffolding to erect and dismantle, saving time and cost.

sections.text: Need Kemnaker-certified TKPK/TKBT training for your team, standby rescue, or extra rope access technicians? Talk to Rope Access Center (RAC), the rope access training and services brand of the Inland group.
